::: {#task .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-studio-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The task</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Produce:</b> a question card of your own, with five realism checks answered, three search strings run and the three closest papers noted.</li>
<li><b>From:</b> six pickers (scale, dimension, system element, lever, stakeholder and an optional twist) that you set yourself or spin.</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> all eight parts of the card are filled in and rated against the rubric, nothing blocks it, and you can say how it differs from the three closest papers.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 40 minutes guided here, then about an hour on your own: run the three searches, skim the first twenty results of each, read the closest abstracts, and revise the card.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">The studio makes no originality judgement. Its checks show which parts are there; rigour is for the rubric, novelty for the literature, and importance for the people who would use the answer.</p>
</div>
<div class="lx-interactive lx-cards" data-learn="r10-question-studio" data-src="../assets/learn/data/r10-question-studio.json ../assets/learn/data/path.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The six pickers</p>
<!-- r10-task:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Picker</th><th scope="col">Options</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Scale</th><td>S0 device and plant · S1 microgrid and community · S2 regional grid · S3 city and region · S4 nation</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Dimension</th><td>Physics and technology · Operations · Planning and optimization · Economics and markets · Techno-economic analysis · LCA and environment · Policy and regulation · Society and livelihoods · Security, resilience and national strategy · Research methods</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">System element</th><td>rooftop solar · heat pumps · EV fleets and school buses · irrigation pumps · cold chains · district heating · industrial process heat · data centers (as a load) · wind farms · utility solar · batteries · long-duration storage · hydrogen · transmission lines · distribution feeders · gas networks · geothermal · hydro · mini-grids · water treatment and desalination · agrivoltaics · building retrofits · demand-response programmes</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Lever</th><td>new technology · operation · market or tariff design · policy · sufficiency (using less) · maintenance and asset life · avoided demand · governance and ownership</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Stakeholder</th><td>low-income renters · homeowners · farmers · rural co-ops · municipal utilities · investor-owned utilities · grid operators · regulators · developers · large energy users · city councils · transit agencies · workers in fossil industries · tribal nations · communities near infrastructure · future generations</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Twist (optional)</th><td>a week-long cold snap · a drought · a heat wave · a fuel-price spike · a one-mineral supply disruption · a policy reversal · a cyber incident · population decline · rapid load growth · a wildfire season · a new tariff design · a doubled interconnection queue</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Five types of question, and a draft for each</p>
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Type</th><th scope="col">Template</th><th scope="col">Draft from the picks</th><th scope="col">Typical methods</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Descriptive</th><td>How much / how often / where …?</td><td>How much does {metric} vary among {stakeholder} with {element} in {scale}{twist}?</td><td>data analysis, accounting, <span class="lx-term" data-term="gis">GIS</span></td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Explanatory</th><td>Why did … happen?</td><td>Why did {metric} change for {stakeholder} after {lever} for {element} in {scale}{twist}?</td><td>statistics, <span class="lx-term" data-term="econometrics">econometrics</span>, case studies, simulation</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Evaluative</th><td>Did … achieve …, compared with …?</td><td>Did {lever} for {element} lead to {goal} for {stakeholder} in {scale}{twist}, compared with […]?</td><td><span class="lx-term" data-term="difference-in-differences">difference-in-differences</span>, matched comparisons, ex-post review</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Predictive</th><td>What will … be, with what uncertainty?</td><td>What will {metric} be for {stakeholder} with {lever} for {element} in {scale}{twist}, and with what uncertainty?</td><td>forecasting, scenarios, <span class="lx-term" data-term="monte-carlo">Monte Carlo</span></td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Prescriptive</th><td>What should [decision-maker] do about … to achieve …, compared with …?</td><td>What should {stakeholder} do about {element} in {scale}, through {lever}, to achieve {goal}{twist}, compared with […]?</td><td><span class="lx-term" data-term="optimization">optimization</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="decision-analysis">decision analysis</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="mcda">MCDA</span></td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p class="lx-hint">Words used here: <span class="lx-term" data-term="energy-burden">energy burden</span> · <span class="lx-term" data-term="customer-hours">customer-hours</span> · <span class="lx-term" data-term="net-present-value">net present value</span> · <span class="lx-term" data-term="techno-economic-analysis">techno-economic analysis</span> · <span class="lx-term" data-term="life-cycle-assessment">LCA</span> (life cycle assessment)</p>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Realism checks: each passes, warns or blocks</p><ul>
<li><strong>Data exist:</strong> Can you name a dataset that measures your metric, at your scale and time step? <em>Note: the dataset, its licence and its date.</em></li>
<li><strong>Physics sanity:</strong> Do the units and sizes make sense: power in MW against energy in MWh, nothing above its rating, energy in balance? <em>Note: one number you checked, with its units.</em></li>
<li><strong>Institutions:</strong> Can you say who pays, who permits, and which jurisdiction's rules apply, as of which date? <em>Note: the rule that applies, and its date.</em></li>
<li><strong>Scope fits the time:</strong> Could a first version be done in the research capstone's 20 to 40 hours, or in the time your project has? <em>Note: what a first version covers.</em></li>
<li><strong>People and ethics:</strong> If people or communities are part of the study, do you know how you will get consent and treat them fairly? <em>Note: your consent plan, or “no people involved”.</em></li>
</ul>
<!-- r10-task:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you pick or spin each part, get a draft for the type you choose, and keep your card in this browser or share it as a link.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="lx-datanote"><span>Drafts, example cards and exemplars are illustrative. The paper counts come from OpenAlex keyword searches (articles and reviews, 2016 to 2 November 2026, retrieved 2 November 2026); they are context only, and the clusters overlap.</span></p>
```
:::

## Two answers to the same task
:::

```{=html}
<div id="r10-exemplars" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The task</p>
<p>Spin: S3 city and region · society and livelihoods · heat pumps · low-income renters · a heat wave. Write a question card.</p>
<!-- r10-exemplars:start (written from the data file by LX.Exemplars' staticHTML, and the example cards from the data file, in the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-ex-cols">
<div class="lx-ex-ans weak"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Weak answer · Developing</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Question:</b> How will heat pumps help [1] low-income renters in heat waves?
<b>Type:</b> predictive
<b>Audience:</b> low-income renters [2]
<b>Metric:</b> comfort [3]
<b>Compared with:</b> (blank) [4]
<b>I would be wrong if:</b> (left blank) [5]
<b>Realism and papers:</b> (not done) [6]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> Help with what? The word hides the metric.</li><li value="2"><b>Falls short:</b> A group, but no use for the answer is stated. Renters could use it; say for what, or name who controls the change.</li><li value="3"><b>Falls short:</b> No units: hours above a safe indoor temperature could be counted.</li><li value="4"><b>Falls short:</b> No <span class="lx-term" data-term="counterfactual">counterfactual</span>: help compared with what?</li><li value="5"><b>Falls short:</b> No falsification statement, so no result could count against it.</li><li value="6"><b>Falls short:</b> No realism review and no closest papers: nobody yet knows whether data exist or what is already known.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong answer · Proficient on framing and realism</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Question:</b> During a week-long heat wave, how many hours above the city's indoor-heat safety threshold would Prairie City's low-income renters avoid if landlords installed heat pumps instead of window air conditioners?
<b>Type:</b> predictive
<b>Audience:</b> the city's housing office, which sets rental standards [1]
<b>Metric:</b> hours above the indoor-heat threshold, per household per heat wave [2]
<b>Compared with:</b> window air conditioners in the same homes [3]
<b>Scale and boundary:</b> S3; renter households in Prairie City; landlords' installation costs left out, and said so [4]
<b>I would be wrong if:</b> heat-pump homes saw no fewer hot hours than homes with window units [5]
<b>Main uncertainty:</b> whether renters can afford to run the cooling during the heat wave [6]
<b>Realism:</b> data warn (few homes have indoor sensors); physics pass; rules pass (the city's 2026 rental code); time pass; people warn (consent for sensors in homes) [7]
<b>Closest papers:</b> three found, each differing (owner-occupied homes; a cooler city; cooling bills, not hot hours) [8]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> A user and the use: the office sets the standards the answer informs. Landlords control the installation; that is a separate line.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> A metric with units, from indoor sensors or a building model.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> A realistic alternative, not “no cooling at all”.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> The boundary names what it leaves out.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> A result that would show the expectation false.</li><li value="6"><b>Works:</b> The uncertainty that could change the answer most, and it comes from the spin's society dimension.</li><li value="7"><b>Works:</b> The five realism checks answered, with the evidence or the reason for each warning.</li><li value="8"><b>Works:</b> How the card differs from each closest paper. The line shows the form of the notes; the papers come from your own searches.</li></ol></div>
</div>
<table class="lx-facts lx-ex-diff"><thead><tr><th scope="col"></th><th scope="col">Weak answer</th><th scope="col">Strong answer</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Metric and units</th><td>“Comfort”</td><td>Hours above a threshold</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Audience</th><td>A group, no use stated</td><td>A user, and what they decide</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Counterfactual</th><td>None</td><td>Window units in the same homes</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Boundary</th><td>Not stated</td><td>Who is counted, what is left out</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Falsification</th><td>None</td><td>A result that would show it wrong</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Realism and papers</th><td>Not done</td><td>Five checks; how it differs from three papers</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Seven example cards</p>
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Combination</th><th scope="col">Type</th><th scope="col">Question</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>S1 · society · community solar · low-income renters</td><td>evaluative</td><td>Did a rural co-op's community-solar programme lower renters' energy burden more than bill credits of the same cost would have?</td></tr>
<tr><td>S0 · operations · irrigation pumps · farmers</td><td>prescriptive</td><td>How much irrigation pumping on a Plains farm could move to windy night hours without lowering yield, and what is that worth under the co-op's tariff?</td></tr>
<tr><td>S3 · security · heat pumps · elderly households · cold snap</td><td>predictive</td><td>During a week-long cold snap, how would all-electric heating change the risk of losing heat for elderly households, with and without backup?</td></tr>
<tr><td>S2 · environment · data-center cooling · nearby communities · drought</td><td>descriptive</td><td>How do the cooling choices of large data centers shift water use and summer peak demand in a water-stressed region?</td></tr>
<tr><td>S4 · security · batteries · regulators · mineral disruption</td><td>predictive, with a prescriptive follow-up</td><td>How sensitive is a national storage build-out to a one-year disruption of one mineral, and which design choices reduce the risk?</td></tr>
<tr><td>S1 · TEA · mini-grids · farmers</td><td>prescriptive</td><td>Which productive uses make a solar mini-grid viable without lowering household access?</td></tr>
<tr><td>S3 · sufficiency · building retrofits · city council</td><td>explanatory</td><td>Why did some neighbourhoods' heating demand fall more than others after a retrofit programme?</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<!-- r10-exemplars:end -->
</div>
</div>
```

::: {#selfcheck .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## Check your own work against the rubric
:::

```{=html}
<div id="r10-rubric" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- r10-rubric:start (written by LX.Rubric's staticHTML, from the course rubric, and the checklist from the data file, in the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts lx-rb-static"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Competence</th><th scope="col">Developing</th><th scope="col">Proficient (the bar)</th><th scope="col">Strong</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Framing<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: all eight parts of the card are filled in, each meets the rubric's words, and the boundary says what is left out.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Question vague or untyped; no audience or counterfactual.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Typed question with audience or decision-maker, metric with units, counterfactual, scale and boundary; one falsification statement.</td><td data-l="Strong">Also explains why the question matters to its audience and what answer would change a decision.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Realism<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: the realism checks answered, with the data's status and a list of what the card leaves out.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Assumes announced projects exist.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Evidence status of key inputs; a 'what the analysis leaves out' list.</td><td data-l="Strong">Realism checked with a practitioner or primary documents.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Before you take a card to a mentor</p>
<ul><li><b>Type:</b> Named, with its template.</li><li><b>Audience:</b> Someone who would use the answer, and for what.</li><li><b>Metric:</b> Measurable, with units.</li><li><b>Counterfactual:</b> A realistic alternative to compare with.</li><li><b>Scale and boundary:</b> Including what is left out.</li><li><b>I would be wrong if…:</b> A result that would count against you.</li><li><b>Main uncertainty:</b> The input that could change the answer most.</li><li><b>Data:</b> One dataset named, with its licence and date.</li><li><b>Rules:</b> Who pays, who permits, which jurisdiction, as of when.</li><li><b>Time:</b> A first version fits the time you have.</li><li><b>People:</b> Consent and fair treatment planned, if people are involved.</li><li><b>Three closest papers:</b> Found, and how your card differs from each.</li></ul>
<!-- r10-rubric:end -->
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="r10-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="few" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If a search finds few papers on a topic, a question about it is new and important.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Few papers can mean other words, other fields, unpublished reports, or a question nobody needs answered; novelty is checked by reading, not by counting.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="many" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If thousands of papers exist on an element, there is nothing left to study.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. A new place, a new group of people, new data or a new twist can each make a question open; the closest papers tell you which.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="block" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A realism block is a reason to change the question, not to drop the topic.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. A different metric, scale or period often turns an unanswerable question into one a first study can answer.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>How much has been written: the counts behind the context line</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">

<li>The search queries are in this page's <a href="../assets/learn/data/r10-question-studio.json">data file</a>.</li>
</ul>

<tr><td>mini-grids and access</td><td class="n">18,711</td><td class="n">1.16</td></tr>
<tr><td>energy security</td><td class="n">18,753</td><td class="n">1.29</td></tr>
<tr><td>hydrogen</td><td class="n">19,174</td><td class="n">4.82</td></tr>
<tr><td>LCA</td><td class="n">22,703</td><td class="n">1.16</td></tr>
<tr><td>electricity markets</td><td class="n">24,138</td><td class="n">0.84</td></tr>
<tr><td>machine learning</td><td class="n">26,451</td><td class="n">4.21</td></tr>
<tr><td>microgrids</td><td class="n">36,753</td><td class="n">1.16</td></tr>
<tr><td>TEA</td><td class="n">38,283</td><td class="n">1.68</td></tr>
<tr><td>batteries and long-duration storage</td><td class="n">53,316</td><td class="n">1.67</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<ul><li>Context only: the clusters overlap, and the counts are not weighted by quality.</li><li>Refreshed yearly with the same queries.</li><li>Few papers is no evidence that a question is new, important or feasible.</li><li>Many papers is no evidence that it is done.</li></ul>
<!-- r10-crowding:end -->
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Researcher</span>From a card to a study</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<p>The research capstone (CR, upcoming) starts from a card made here.</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="r02-literature.html">R2</a> maps the literature around it.</li>
<li><a href="r03-system-and-method.html">R3</a> chooses the system, boundary and method.</li>
<li>The later studios cover data, verification, uncertainty, accounting, communication and integrity.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>What this studio leaves out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>The pickers are a starting point, not a map of every possible study: you can type any question onto the card.</li>
<li>The realism checks are your own answers; the studio cannot see your data or your rules.</li>
<li>The search strings are a first pass in one open database. Other databases, other words and other languages find other papers.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
